\begin{theorem}[Degree of a cube monomial]
\lean{FABL.fourierDegree_monomial}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p028-b001}
\label{FABL.fourierDegree_monomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff_monomial, FABL.fourierDegree, FABL.fourierDegree_le_iff, FABL.mem_fourierSupport, FABL.monomial}
\difficulty{4}
For every subset $S\\subseteq[n]$, the Fourier degree of the monomial
$x\\mapsto\\prod_{i\\in S}x_i$ on the Boolean cube is exactly $|S|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of full parity]
\lean{FABL.fourierDegree_parityFunction_univ}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p028-b001
}
\label{FABL.fourierDegree_parityFunction_univ}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierDegree, FABL.fourierDegree_monomial, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_toReal}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, the function on the Boolean cube given by the product of
all its coordinates, $x\\mapsto\\prod_{i=1}^n x_i$, has Fourier degree exactly $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sign of a coordinate sum]
\lean{FABL.signEncode_coordinateSum}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b004}
\label{FABL.signEncode_coordinateSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.coordinateSum, FABL.signEncode, FABL.signEncode_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a subset of $\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$, and let
$x=(x_0,\\ldots,x_{n-1})\\in\\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Define $\\sigma(b)=(-1)^b\\in\\{\\pm1\\}$
for $b\\in\\mathbb{F}_2$. Then $\\sigma\\left(\\sum_{i\\in S}x_i\\right)=\\prod_{i\\in
S}\\sigma(x_i)$, where the sum is taken in $\\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Encoding a parity function]
\lean{FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding_parityFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binarySignEquiv, FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding, FABL.coordinateSum, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.signEncode, FABL.signEncode_booleanFunctionF₂Encoding, FABL.signEncode_coordinateSum}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b001
}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $S$ be a subset of its coordinates. The binary
encoding of the sign parity function on $S$ is the function that sums the input bits
indexed by $S$ in $\mathbb F_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Dot product with a set indicator vector]
\lean{FABL.f₂DotProduct_f₂CubeOfFinset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.coordinateSum, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset_apply, FABL.f₂DotProduct}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $S$ be a subset of its coordinate indices, and let
$x\in\bbr_2^n$. The dot product of $x$ with the indicator vector of $S$ equals the sum
of the coordinates of $x$ indexed by $S$, with the sum taken in $\bbr_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Full-coordinate monomial]
\lean{FABL.f₂AndFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.anfMonomial}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p013-b008,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b003
}
For each $n\\ge 0$, define the function on $\\mathbb F_2^n$ given by the monomial
containing every coordinate, namely $x\\mapsto\\prod_{i=1}^n x_i$ in $\\mathbb F_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Product formula for the AND function]
\lean{FABL.f₂AndFunction_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.anfMonomial, FABL.f₂AndFunction}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b003}
\difficulty{1}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every binary vector $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the AND
function on $x$ equals the product of all its coordinates:
$\operatorname{AND}(x)=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Algebraic degree of the full monomial]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_f₂AndFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_anfMonomial, FABL.f₂AndFunction}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $n$, the function from $n$-bit vectors over the field with
two elements to that field given by the product of all coordinates has algebraic degree
$n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Binary inner product of joined blocks]
\lean{FABL.innerProductModTwoBit_joinF₂CubeBlocks_eq_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit_joinF₂CubeBlocks, FABL.joinF₂CubeBlocks}
\difficulty{3}
For any natural number $n$ and vectors $x,y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the inner product modulo
two of the vector formed by joining $x$ and $y$ is $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i$ in
$\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monomial expansion of the inner product bit]
\lean{FABL.innerProductModTwoBit_eq_sum_anfMonomial}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b003}
\label{FABL.innerProductModTwoBit_eq_sum_anfMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.anfMonomial, FABL.f₂CubeBlockEquiv, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit_joinF₂CubeBlocks_eq_sum, FABL.joinF₂CubeBlocks}
\difficulty{5}
For every natural number $n$, the inner product modulo two on a pair of
Boolean-coordinate vectors of length $n$ is the sum over $i<n$ of the monomial given by
the product of the two coordinates in position $i$, with the sum and products taken in
$\mathbb F_2$.
\end{theorem}
